# Amos Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 335v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Listen to this message that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel — against the entire family I brought up from the land of Egypt:

**2** "Out of all the families on the face of the earth, I have been intimate with you alone. That is why I must punish you for all your sins."

**3** Can two people walk together without agreeing to meet? **4** Does a lion roar in the forest unless he has caught his prey? Does a young lion growl in his den unless he has made a kill? **5** Does a bird drop into a trap unless there's bait in it? Does a trap spring shut unless something trips it? **6** When a trumpet sounds an alarm in a city, don't the people tremble? When disaster strikes a city, hasn't the LORD caused it?

**7** Indeed, the Sovereign LORD never does anything without first revealing his plans to his servants the prophets.

**8** The lion has roared — who isn't afraid? The Sovereign LORD has spoken — who can refuse to proclaim his message?

**9** Shout this from the rooftops of the fortresses in Ashdod and Egypt: "Come and look at the chaos and oppression in Samaria! Gather on the hills around Samaria and witness the outrageous things happening there!"

**10** "My people have forgotten how to do the right thing," says the LORD. "Their fortresses are stuffed with wealth taken by violence and theft."

**11** Therefore, this is what the Sovereign LORD says: "An enemy is coming! He will surround your land, tear down your defenses, and plunder your fortresses."

**12** This is what the LORD says: "A shepherd who tries to rescue a sheep from a lion's mouth will recover only two legs or a piece of an ear. So it will be for the Israelites living in Samaria — they'll be left with nothing but the corner of a couch and a scrap of a bed."

**13** "Now listen and testify against the descendants of Jacob," says the Lord GOD, the God of Heaven's Armies:

**14** "On the day I punish Israel for its sins, I will destroy the pagan altars at Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground. **15** And I will destroy the beautiful homes of the wealthy — their winter mansions and summer houses. Their palatial ivory-paneled homes will be demolished, and all their luxurious houses will be torn down," says the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"You only have I known" (v.2):** This verse demolishes every theology of cheap election. Israel assumed that being "chosen" meant being protected. Amos inverts it: being known by God means being held to a *higher* standard. Privilege brings accountability, not immunity.

**The seven questions (vv.3-6):** Amos uses common-sense cause-and-effect reasoning — lions don't roar without prey, traps don't spring without triggers — to establish one devastating conclusion: when disaster comes to a city, God is behind it. He is not arguing that God is cruel. He is arguing that what is about to happen to Israel is not random misfortune but divine judgment — and it has a cause.

*— PNEUMA*
